_note: Ottawa drop-off sites, researched Nov 2026. verify=true: found on a third-party list or an older page, so call before relying on it. Coordinates from OpenStreetMap. 'accepts' must only list what the site really takes: the app sends people to the nearest site for that type.

sites.name: Trail Waste Facility
sites.notes: City of Ottawa landfill. Electronics are free year-round (ottawa.ca). Batteries, paint, propane and other household hazardous waste only on the City's one-day drop-off event days.

sites.name: Electronic Recycling Association
sites.notes: Takes computers, monitors, TVs and other electronics in any condition (era.ca). Fees for some items (TVs, microwaves). Hours not posted: call 613-518-4467.

sites.name: Quantum Lifecycle Partners
sites.notes: Free residential electronics drop-off, Mon-Fri 7:00-15:30 (quantumlifecycle.com, page from 2025).

sites.name: Best Buy Ottawa East
sites.notes: Store page lists electronics and battery recycling, even for things not bought there (stores.bestbuy.ca).

sites.name: Best Buy Express Rideau Centre
sites.notes: Store page lists battery and electronics recycling (stores.bestbuy.ca, page from 2024). Small store: best for phones, cables, small devices.

sites.name: Best Buy Ottawa West
sites.notes: Listed as a drop-off point by a recycling directory; Best Buy Canada stores generally take electronics and batteries.

sites.name: Best Buy Kanata
sites.notes: Listed as a drop-off point by a recycling directory; Best Buy Canada stores generally take electronics and batteries.

sites.name: The Home Depot Barrhaven
sites.notes: Call2Recycle drop-off for rechargeable and single-use batteries (locations.call2recycle.ca).

sites.name: IKEA Ottawa
sites.notes: IKEA Canada takes back batteries and light bulbs (not fluorescent tubes) at every store. Listed for batteries only, because 'hazardous' here also means paint and propane, which IKEA doesn't take.
